title: Specialty Model Prospectivity Playbook and Procurement Experiment Canvas
creator: Lina Patel
description:
Goal: Produce a lightweight, repeatable playbook and experiment canvas that lets Product and Procurement rapidly evaluate 'specialty' (narrow-domain) LLMs for Redwood customers and map them to provisioning strategies (hosted, dedicated, private). The playbook will combine qualitative buyer signals, microbenchmarks (latency, cost/token, failure modes), kernel/hardware affinity notes, and procurement trigger thresholds.

Why now: Emergent vendor models and domain specialists are appearing frequently in verticals (legal, medical summaries, code generation for internal DSLs). Customers ask for guidance on when to adopt a niche model versus applying Redwood routing/fallback policies to a broader model. Our competitors are surfacing specialized models in catalogs without operational economics; we can win by offering a fast 'prospectivity' signal that translates to procurement and runtime actions.

Scope:
- Define a prospectivity scoring rubric combining: buyer fit, latency sensitivity, quantization readiness, kernel/hardware affinity, reliability signals, and substitute-cost delta.
- Create a 6x6 experiment canvas for each model candidate (workload slices x deployment modes) with measurable success metrics.
- Run an initial field experiment on 6 candidate models across two vertical workloads (legal summarization, finance reconciliation) and two regions (us-west, eu-central).
- Produce a procurement trigger sheet (rules for when PM/Procurement should recommend reservation vs. hosted adoption) and a tech-runbook for quick onboarding tests (bench harness, data hygiene checklist).

Constraints & non-goals:
- This ticket focuses on the decision framework and an initial evidence set; full vendor integrations or contract negotiations are out of scope.
- We will not certify models for enterprise SLA in this experiment—only provide procurement recommendations and ops checklists.
deliverables: Experiment canvas template (6x6) and one completed canvas per model tested
Microbenchmark harness config and synthetic workloads (repository link)
Procurement trigger sheet with threshold rules
Field notes: 6 candidate model dossiers with hardware affinity and quantization notes
Presentation to GTM and Procurement with recommended pilots
acceptance_criteria: Rubric documented and reviewed by Research and Procurement
At least 6 completed experiment canvases with raw telemetry attached
Bench harness reproduces latency/cost numbers within +/- 10% across two runs
Procurement trigger sheet lists clear decision boundaries and person-owners for escalation
GTM pilot slate and next-step recommendations accepted by PM director
